data.name: Barzakh
data.gender_notes: Barzakh is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic eschatology, Barzakh refers to a barrier or an intervening state between the worldly life and the afterlife, or between the death and resurrection. The name Barzakh carries the meaning “Barrier or Intervening State” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Barzakh usually hope their child will grow to embody barrier or intervening state and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: As mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Mu'minun, 23:100), Barzakh is a state where souls are held accountable before proceeding to the afterlife.
data.etymology: Barzakh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Barrier or Intervening State.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barzakh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The concept of Barzakh is a fascinating and intriguing one in Islamic culture, as it signifies a liminal space between two worlds - the temporal world we inhabit in our daily lives, and the eternal world that awaits us after death. It is a reminder of the transient nature of our existence in this world and the ultimate reality of the afterlife. Many poets and philosophers have explored the theme of Barzakh in their works, providing a rich literary and artistic tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: The idea of Barzakh holds great significance in the spiritual journey of a believer. It emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and righteousness in this life to ensure a peaceful and rewarding existence in the hereafter. The intervening state is often seen as a testing ground for the soul, a place where the deeds and actions of one's life are weighed and evaluated. The belief in Barzakh serves as a powerful motivator for individuals to strive towards spiritual growth and betterment, while also providing comfort and hope in the face of the inevitable separation from the temporal world.
